recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-11309; future MolecularDefinition molecule-typing refinements should be handled as new Clinical Genomics/MolecularDefinition work.
issue_request: FHIR-11309 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 Clinical Genomics request for the old FHIR-core Sequence resource. It asked to clarify Sequence.type so AA, DNA, and RNA were described as amino acid sequence, DNA sequence, and messenger/RNA sequence instead of the ambiguous 'Amino acid / cDNA transcript / RNA variant' wording.
initial_application: Commit 5ab7990995a9c5fbfdd33e99aa5e7b2aa72a7816, explicitly tagged '#11309 #11310 Revise definition on Sequence.quantity and Sequence.type', changed source/sequence/sequence-spreadsheet.xml from the ambiguous Sequence.type definition to 'Amino Acid Sequence/ DNA Sequence / RNA Sequence'.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini lists Sequence under removed resources, omits Sequence and MolecularSequence from the active [resources] list, and comments MolecularSequence in current classification sections. Current diagnostics/genomics narrative points to MolecularDefinition in Clinical Genomics incubator content, and the successor MolecularDefinition source separates broad moleculeType values such as DNA/RNA/amino acid from finer type classifications such as mRNA/siRNA. Later Jira/community searches did not find a FHIR-11309 reversal or a current-core requirement to reintroduce DSTU2 Sequence.type wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit with no source changes. A source edit would either touch retired/out-of-build Sequence material or broaden this old Sequence tracker into current MolecularDefinition policy, which the evidence does not support.

related_jiras.note: The same 2016 source commit also revised Sequence.quantity, and the combined branch already contains a separate FHIR-11310 audit commit.
A later Published R5 MolecularSequence issue adjusted relative sequence details but did not change or reverse the Sequence.type clarification.
